## Data {#sec-appendix-data}

This section reports the estimation samples and the descriptive tables referred to in @sec-data.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-sample-flow
#| tbl-cap: "Estimation samples."
#| echo: false

sample_row <- function(analysis, sample, unit, waves, m, data) {
  d <- data[fixest::obs(m), ]
  tibble::tibble(
    Analysis = analysis,
    Sample = sample,
    Unit = unit,
    Waves = waves,
    Observations = format(nobs(m), big.mark = ","),
    Individuals = format(dplyr::n_distinct(d$xwaveid), big.mark = ","),
    `Low-English individuals` = format(
      dplyr::n_distinct(d$xwaveid[d$origin_group %in% "mnes_loweng"]), big.mark = ","
    )
  )
}

dplyr::bind_rows(
  sample_row("Employee wages", "Employees", "Person-year", "1 to 21", regression1_v1a, data_regression_1),
  sample_row("Owner income and risk", "Restricted pairs (same status)", "Person-pair", "1 to 21", regression2_income, data_regression_2_pairs),
  sample_row("Owner income and risk", "Unrestricted pairs", "Person-pair", "1 to 21", regression2_income_unrestricted, data_regression_2_unrestricted),
  sample_row("Entry into ownership", "Non-owners at t−1", "Person-pair", "1 to 24", regression3_v4a, data_regression_3)
) |>
  tinytable::tt() |>
  tinytable::theme_empty() |>
  tinytable::style_tt(i = 0, line = "tb") |>
  tinytable::style_tt(i = 4, line = "b") |>
  tinytable::style_tt(j = 1:4, align = "l") |>
  tinytable::style_tt(j = 5:7, align = "c")
```

::: {.notes}
*Notes:* This table reports the estimation sample of each analysis. Observations and individuals are those of the main specification, namely the Type 0 column of @tbl-b1-main for employee wages, the income regressions of @tbl-b2-main for owner income and risk, and the *Adding human capital* column of @tbl-b3-main for entry into ownership. A person-pair is an individual observed in two consecutive waves, $t-1$ and $t$. Unrestricted pairs classify everyone who is an employee, owner with employees or own-account worker at $t$ by their status at $t$; restricted pairs also require the same status at $t-1$. Low-English individuals are MNES migrants with low English proficiency.
:::

```{r}
#| label: tbl-firmtype
#| tbl-cap: "Distribution of firm structures observed in the employee sample."
#| echo: false

fmt_n <- function(x) format(x, big.mark = ",", trim = TRUE)
fmt_num <- function(x, d = 2) {
  formatC(x, format = "f", digits = d, big.mark = ",")
}
firm_base <- employee_sample |> filter(wave <= 21L)

tibble::tibble(
  Category = c(
    "Small single-site",
    "Chain-like",
    "Small-site chain",
    "None of the three",
    "Firm structure missing"
  ),
  n = c(
    sum(firm_base$small_single_site == 1L, na.rm = TRUE),
    sum(firm_base$chain_like == 1L, na.rm = TRUE),
    sum(firm_base$small_site_chain == 1L, na.rm = TRUE),
    sum(
      coalesce(firm_base$small_single_site, 0L) +
        coalesce(firm_base$chain_like, 0L) +
        coalesce(firm_base$small_site_chain, 0L) ==
        0L &
        !is.na(firm_base$small_single_site)
    ),
    sum(is.na(firm_base$small_single_site))
  )
) |>
  mutate(
    `Person-years` = fmt_n(n),
    `Share (%)` = fmt_num(100 * n / nrow(firm_base), 1)
  ) |>
  select(-n) |>
  tt(
    width = c(0.40, 0.30, 0.30)
  ) |>
  style_tt(j = 2:3, align = "r") |>
  style_tt(i = 0, bold = TRUE, align = "c") |>
  style_tt(i = 0, line = "b", line_width = 0.05)
```

::: {.notes}
*Notes:* This table reports the distribution of workplace types (@sec-data-workplace) across employee person-years in HILDA waves 1 to 21. The categories are mutually exclusive. Small single-site and small-site chain workplaces have fewer than 20 people at the workplace and an employer with one or several locations respectively; chain-like workplaces have 20 or more people and an employer with at least 500 employees nationally. *None of the three* is the reference category of other large workplaces, and *Firm structure missing* means that workplace size or the number of locations is unanswered. The base is every employee person-year before observations with missing wages or controls are dropped, so the total exceeds the wage sample in @tbl-sample-flow.
:::

```{r}
#| label: tbl-share-dist
#| tbl-cap: "Distribution of the leave-one-out ownership exposure shares across industry-year (waves 1-21)."
#| echo: false
SHARE_SUFFIX <- "1d_type0"
fmt_n <- function(x) format(x, big.mark = ",", trim = TRUE)
fmt_num <- function(x, d = 2) {
  formatC(x, format = "f", digits = d, big.mark = ",")
}
sv <- function(stem) paste0(stem, "_", SHARE_SUFFIX)

cell_shares <- panel_final |>
  filter(!is.na(industry_19categories_jbmi61), !wave %in% 22:24) |>
  summarise(
    across(
      all_of(c(sv("loo_mes"), sv("loo_mnes_higheng"), sv("loo_mnes_loweng"))),
      ~ first(.x[!is.na(.x)])
    ),
    n_owners = first(.data[[sv("n_owners")]]),
    .by = c(industry_19categories_jbmi61, wave)
  )

owner_group_map <- c(
  "MES" = "mes",
  "MNES (high English proficiency)" = "mnes_higheng",
  "MNES (low English proficiency)" = "mnes_loweng"
)

owner_counts <- purrr::imap_dfr(owner_group_map, function(grp, lab) {
  owners_grp <- panel_final |>
    filter(
      is_owner == 1L,
      origin_group == grp,
      !is.na(industry_19categories_jbmi61),
      !wave %in% 22:24
    )
  tibble::tibble(
    Share = lab,
    Owners = n_distinct(owners_grp$xwaveid)
  )
})

share_map <- c(
  "MES" = sv("loo_mes"),
  "MNES (high English proficiency)" = sv("loo_mnes_higheng"),
  "MNES (low English proficiency)" = sv("loo_mnes_loweng")
)

purrr::imap_dfr(share_map, function(v, lab) {
  x <- cell_shares[[v]]
  x <- x[!is.na(x)]
  tibble::tibble(
    Share = lab,
    `Industry-year (N)` = fmt_n(length(x)),
    `Zero (%)` = fmt_num(100 * mean(x == 0), 3),
    Mean = fmt_num(mean(x), 3),
    SD = fmt_num(sd(x), 3),
    Median = fmt_num(median(x), 3),
    Max = fmt_num(max(x), 3)
  )
}) |>
  left_join(owner_counts, by = "Share") |>
  relocate(Share, Owners, `Industry-year (N)`) |>
  mutate(Owners = fmt_n(Owners)) |>
  tt(
    width = c(0.30, 0.10, 0.12, 0.10, 0.10, 0.09, 0.09, 0.10)
  ) |>
  style_tt(j = 1, align = "l") |>
  style_tt(j = 2:8, align = "r") |>
  style_tt(i = 0, align = "c") |>
  style_tt(i = 0, line = "b", line_width = 0.05)
```

::: {.notes}
*Notes:* This table reports the distribution of the leave-one-out owner shares of @eq-loo-shares, without decay (Type 0), across industry-year cells in HILDA waves 1 to 21. *Owners* is the number of distinct owners in each origin group. *Industry-year (N)* counts the cells with at least one owner; 27 of the 399 possible cells have no owners and are excluded because the share is undefined. *Zero (%)* is the percentage of cells with no owner from the group.
:::

```{r}
#| label: tbl-owner-industry
#| tbl-cap: "Industry composition of business owners (%) by origin and English proficiency group."
#| echo: false
owner_base <- panel_final |>
  filter(
    is_owner == 1L,
    !is.na(industry_19categories_jbmi61),
    !is.na(origin_group)
  )

owner_counts <- owner_base |>
  summarise(n_obs = n(), n_persons = n_distinct(xwaveid), .by = origin_group) |>
  pivot_longer(c(n_obs, n_persons), names_to = "Industry", values_to = "v") |>
  mutate(
    Industry = if_else(Industry == "n_obs", "Person-years", "Persons"),
    v = format(v, big.mark = ",", trim = TRUE)
  ) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = origin_group, values_from = v)

owner_base |>
  mutate(
    industry_19categories_jbmi61 = stringr::str_replace(
      as.character(industry_19categories_jbmi61),
      "^\\w",
      toupper
    )
  ) |>
  summarise(n = n(), .by = c(industry_19categories_jbmi61, origin_group)) |>
  mutate(pct = 100 * n / sum(n), .by = origin_group) |>
  select(-n) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = origin_group, values_from = pct, values_fill = 0) |>
  rename(Industry = industry_19categories_jbmi61) |>
  arrange(desc(native)) |>
  mutate(across(-Industry, ~ sprintf("%.2f", .x))) |>
  bind_rows(owner_counts) |>
  rename(
    `Native-born` = native,
    MES = mes,
    `High English` = mnes_higheng,
    `Low English` = mnes_loweng
  ) |>
  relocate(Industry, `Native-born`, MES, `High English`, `Low English`) |>
  tt(width = c(0.30, 0.18, 0.12, 0.20, 0.20)) |>
  group_tt(j = list("MNES" = 4:5), bold = FALSE) |>
  style_tt(j = 2:5, align = "c") |>
  style_tt(i = 0, j = 1, bold = FALSE, align = "l") |>
  style_tt(i = 0, j = 2:5, bold = FALSE, align = "c") |>
  style_tt(i = 20:21, italic = FALSE, bold = FALSE) |>
  style_tt(i = 19, line = "b", line_width = 0.05) |>
  style_tt(i = 0, line = "b", line_width = 0.05)
```

::: {.notes}
*Notes:* This table reports the percentage of business owners (employers and own-account workers) in each origin group who work in each industry, pooled over HILDA waves 1 to 24. Industries are the 19 ANZSIC divisions, and each column sums to 100. The bottom rows give owner person-years and distinct owners; these are slightly below the counts in @tbl-owner-desc because owners without a reported industry are excluded. *High English* and *Low English* are MNES migrants with high and low English proficiency.
:::

```{r}
#| label: tbl-industry-composition
#| tbl-cap: "Industry composition by worker type."
#| echo: false
ind_base <- panel_final |>
  filter(!is.na(industry_19categories_jbmi61)) |>
  mutate(
    industry_19categories_jbmi61 = stringr::str_replace(
      as.character(industry_19categories_jbmi61),
      "^\\w",
      toupper
    ),
    Group = case_when(
      owner_with_employees == 1L ~ "Self-employed worker with employees",
      own_account_worker == 1L ~ "Own-account worker",
      is_employee == 1L ~ "Employees",
      .default = NA_character_
    )
  ) |>
  filter(!is.na(Group))

ind_counts <- ind_base |>
  summarise(n_obs = n(), n_persons = n_distinct(xwaveid), .by = Group) |>
  pivot_longer(c(n_obs, n_persons), names_to = "Industry", values_to = "v") |>
  mutate(
    Industry = if_else(Industry == "n_obs", "Person-years", "Persons"),
    v = format(v, big.mark = ",", trim = TRUE)
  ) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = Group, values_from = v)

ind_base |>
  summarise(n = n(), .by = c(industry_19categories_jbmi61, Group)) |>
  mutate(pct = 100 * n / sum(n), .by = Group) |>
  select(-n) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = Group, values_from = pct, values_fill = 0) |>
  rename(Industry = industry_19categories_jbmi61) |>
  arrange(desc(`Self-employed worker with employees`)) |>
  mutate(across(-Industry, ~ sprintf("%.1f", .x))) |>
  bind_rows(ind_counts) |>
  relocate(
    Industry,
    Employees,
    `Self-employed worker with employees`,
    `Own-account worker`
  ) |>
  tt(width = c(0.32, 0.13, 0.35, 0.20)) |>
  style_tt(j = 2:4, align = "c") |>
  style_tt(i = 0, j = 1, bold = FALSE, align = "l") |>
  style_tt(i = 0, j = 2:4, bold = FALSE, align = "r") |>
  style_tt(i = 20:21, italic = FALSE, bold = FALSE) |>
  style_tt(i = 19, line = "b", line_width = 0.1) |>
  style_tt(i = 0, line = "b", line_width = 0.05)
```

::: {.notes}
*Notes:* This table reports the percentage of employees, employers (self-employed with employees) and own-account workers (self-employed without employees) who work in each industry, pooled over HILDA waves 1 to 24. Industries are the 19 ANZSIC divisions, ordered by the share of employers, and each column sums to 100. The bottom rows give person-years and distinct individuals in each group.
:::

```{r}
#| label: tbl-panel
#| tbl-cap: "Panel persistence of all respondents by origin group."
#| echo: false

# Waves in which each person is interviewed, for every respondent (owners and
# non-owners), since panel persistence affects every sample that needs
# consecutive waves
panel_final |>
  filter(!is.na(origin_group), !is.na(lf_status_detail_esdtl)) |>
  summarise(
    n_waves = dplyr::n_distinct(wave),
    adjacent = max(as.integer(wave)) - min(as.integer(wave)) + 1L == dplyr::n_distinct(wave),
    .by = c(xwaveid, origin_group)
  ) |>
  summarise(
    Persons = n(),
    `Mean waves` = mean(n_waves),
    `Median waves` = median(n_waves),
    `1 wave (%)` = 100 * mean(n_waves == 1),
    `10+ waves (%)` = 100 * mean(n_waves >= 10),
    `Adjacent (%)` = 100 * mean(adjacent),
    `All waves (%)` = 100 * mean(n_waves == 24),
    .by = origin_group
  ) |>
  rename(Group = origin_group) |>
  mutate(
    Group = recode_values(
      Group,
      "native" ~ "Native-born",
      "mes" ~ "MES",
      "mnes_higheng" ~ "MNES (high English)",
      "mnes_loweng" ~ "MNES (low English)"
    )
  ) |>
  arrange(match(
    Group,
    c("Native-born", "MES", "MNES (high English)", "MNES (low English)")
  )) |>
  tt(
    width = c(0.19, 0.10, 0.12, 0.13, 0.10, 0.12, 0.12, 0.12)
  ) |>
  format_tt(j = 2, digits = 0, num_fmt = "decimal", num_mark_big = ",") |>
  format_tt(j = 3:4, digits = 2, num_fmt = "decimal") |>
  format_tt(j = 5:8, digits = 1, num_fmt = "decimal") |>
  style_tt(j = 2:8, align = "r") |>
  style_tt(j = 1, bold = FALSE, align = "l") |>
  style_tt(i = 0, line = "b", line_width = 0.05)
```

::: {.notes}
*Notes:* This table reports the panel persistence of every respondent, owners and non-owners, by origin group, counting the waves (out of 24) in which each person is interviewed. *1 wave (%)* and *10+ waves (%)* are the percentages interviewed in only one wave and in ten or more waves, *Adjacent (%)* the percentage whose interviews form one unbroken run of consecutive waves and *All waves (%)* the percentage interviewed in all 24 waves. Samples that need consecutive waves, such as the owner income and entry samples, lose more people from groups with less persistent participation.
:::

## Employee Wages {#sec-appendix-b1}

This section reports the distribution of the owner shares, the full estimates behind @tbl-b1-main and the robustness and sensitivity checks discussed in @sec-results-block1. It also reports two further robustness checks, inference that allows for correlation within industries (@sec-appendix-wild), and owner shares built with the longitudinal survey weight (@sec-appendix-lnw).

```{r}
#| label: tbl-loo-shares-b1
#| tbl-cap: "Distribution of the leave-one-out owner shares across employees in the wage sample."
#| echo: false
summary_data <- data_regression_1 |>
  select(
    loo_mes_1d_type0,
    loo_mnes_higheng_1d_type0,
    loo_mnes_loweng_1d_type0,
    loo_mes_1d_type1,
    loo_mnes_higheng_1d_type1,
    loo_mnes_loweng_1d_type1,
    loo_mes_1d_type2,
    loo_mnes_higheng_1d_type2,
    loo_mnes_loweng_1d_type2
  ) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "var", values_to = "v") |>
  filter(!is.na(v)) |>
  tidyr::separate(var, into = c("share_type", "decay_type"), sep = "_1d_") |>
  summarise(
    Mean = mean(v),
    `Std. Dev.` = sd(v),
    `Q1` = quantile(v, 0.25),
    Median = median(v),
    `Q3` = quantile(v, 0.75),
    Max = max(v),
    `% Zero` = 100 * mean(v == 0),
    .by = c(share_type, decay_type)
  ) |>
  mutate(
    share_type = recode_values(
      share_type,
      "loo_mes" ~ "MES owner density",
      "loo_mnes_higheng" ~ "MNES high English owner density",
      "loo_mnes_loweng" ~ "MNES low English owner density"
    ),
    decay_type = recode_values(
      decay_type,
      "type0" ~ "Type 0 (no weighting)",
      "type1" ~ "Type 1 (pooled - same λ applied to all migrants)",
      "type2" ~ "Type 2 (λ is split by migrant origin group)"
    )
  ) |>
  arrange(
    factor(
      decay_type,
      levels = c(
        "Type 0 (no weighting)",
        "Type 1 (pooled - same λ applied to all migrants)",
        "Type 2 (λ is split by migrant origin group)"
      )
    ),
    share_type
  )

bind_rows(
  tibble(
    Density = "Type 0 (no weighting)",
    Mean = NA_real_,
    `Std. Dev.` = NA_real_,
    `Q1` = NA_real_,
    Median = NA_real_,
    `Q3` = NA_real_,
    Max = NA_real_,
    `% Zero` = NA_real_
  ),
  summary_data |>
    filter(decay_type == "Type 0 (no weighting)") |>
    select(
      Density = share_type,
      Mean,
      `Std. Dev.`,
      `Q1`,
      Median,
      `Q3`,
      Max,
      `% Zero`
    ),
  tibble(
    Density = "Type 1 (pooled - same λ applied to all migrants)",
    Mean = NA_real_,
    `Std. Dev.` = NA_real_,
    `Q1` = NA_real_,
    Median = NA_real_,
    `Q3` = NA_real_,
    Max = NA_real_,
    `% Zero` = NA_real_
  ),
  summary_data |>
    filter(decay_type == "Type 1 (pooled - same λ applied to all migrants)") |>
    select(
      Density = share_type,
      Mean,
      `Std. Dev.`,
      `Q1`,
      Median,
      `Q3`,
      Max,
      `% Zero`
    ),
  tibble(
    Density = "Type 2 (λ is split by migrant origin group)",
    Mean = NA_real_,
    `Std. Dev.` = NA_real_,
    `Q1` = NA_real_,
    Median = NA_real_,
    `Q3` = NA_real_,
    Max = NA_real_,
    `% Zero` = NA_real_
  ),
  summary_data |>
    filter(decay_type == "Type 2 (λ is split by migrant origin group)") |>
    select(
      Density = share_type,
      Mean,
      `Std. Dev.`,
      `Q1`,
      Median,
      `Q3`,
      Max,
      `% Zero`
    )
) |>
  mutate(across(2:8, ~ ifelse(is.na(.), NA, sprintf(if (cur_column() == "% Zero") "%.1f" else "%.3f", .)))) |>
  mutate(across(2:8, as.character)) |>
  mutate(across(2:8, ~ replace_na(., ""))) |>
  tt() |>
  style_tt(i = c(1, 5, 9), italic = TRUE) |>
  style_tt(i = 0, line = "tb", bold = FALSE)
```

::: {.notes}
*Notes:* This table reports the distribution of the leave-one-out owner shares of @eq-loo-shares across employee person-years in the wage sample of @tbl-b1-main, so each employee contributes the share of their own industry and year. The shares run from 0 to 1. Q1 and Q3 are the 25th and 75th percentiles, and *% Zero* is the percentage of person-years whose share is exactly zero. Type 0 applies no decay, Type 1 a pooled decay rate ($\lambda = `r lambda_mean`$) and Type 2 origin-specific rates ($\lambda_{\text{MES}} = `r lambda_mes`$ and $\lambda_{\text{MNES}} = `r lambda_other`$).
:::

::: {.notes}
*Notes:* This table reports OLS estimates of @eq-employee-wage with small workplaces defined as having fewer than 10, 20 (the baseline of @tbl-b1-main) or 50 people. The dependent variable is the log hourly wage in the employee's main job. Each column represents a different size threshold, which applies to both small single-site and small-site chain workplaces, and all columns use the owner shares without decay (Type 0). All columns include covariates for age, sex, origin group, casual or permanent employment, occupation, education, SEIFA decile, occupational tenure, employer tenure and union membership, and year, industry-year and state-year fixed effects. Reference categories are managers and administrators (occupation), Year 11 or below (education), native-born (origin), casual employment and no union membership. The F-statistic, with its degrees of freedom in parentheses, tests the null hypothesis that the three owner-share interactions are jointly zero, using the clustered covariance matrix; its p-value is reported in the row below. All standard errors reported in parentheses are clustered at the individual and industry-year levels. ∗ p < 0.10, ∗∗ p < 0.05, ∗∗∗ p < 0.01.
:::

```{r}
#| label: tbl-b1-placebo
#| tbl-cap: "Owner density interacted with chain workplaces."
#| echo: false

share_labels <- c(
  loo_mes = "MES owner density",
  loo_mnes_higheng = "MNES high-English owner density",
  loo_mnes_loweng = "MNES low-English owner density"
)
site_labels <- c(
  small_single_site = "Small single-site",
  small_site_chain = "Small-site chain",
  chain_like = "Chain-like"
)

# One row per workplace type x share, merged across the three decay types
coef_b1_placebo <- unlist(lapply(names(site_labels), \(w) {
  unlist(lapply(names(share_labels), \(s) {
    setNames(
      rep(paste(site_labels[[w]], "x", share_labels[[s]]), 3),
      paste0(w, ":", s, "_1d_type", 0:2)
    )
  }))
}))

b1_placebo_layout <- b1_full_layout(c(
  "Firm structure" = 3,
  "Main interactions" = 3,
  "Small sites of multi-site employers" = 3,
  "Chain-like workplaces" = 3
))

placebo_joint_p <- \(m, w) fmt_p(fixest::wald(m, keep = paste0("^", w, ":loo_"), print = FALSE)$p)

modelsummary::modelsummary(
  setNames(regression1_placebo, c("No decay (Type 0)", "Pooled decay (Type 1)", "Origin-specific decay (Type 2)")),
  coef_map = c(site_labels, coef_b1_placebo, b1_controls),
  gof_map = gof_comma(tribble(
    ~raw,   ~clean,         ~fmt,
    "nobs", "Observations (person-years)", 0
  )),
  estimate = "{estimate}{stars}",
  statistic = "({std.error})",
  stars = thesis_stars,
  fmt = modelsummary::fmt_decimal(digits = 3, big.mark = ","),
  add_rows = tibble::tibble(
    term = c("Individuals", "Joint test, small-site chain (p-value)", "Joint test, chain-like (p-value)"),
    `No decay (Type 0)` = c(fmt_int(n_individuals_model(regression1_placebo$type0)), placebo_joint_p(regression1_placebo$type0, "small_site_chain"), placebo_joint_p(regression1_placebo$type0, "chain_like")),
    `Pooled decay (Type 1)` = c(fmt_int(n_individuals_model(regression1_placebo$type1)), placebo_joint_p(regression1_placebo$type1, "small_site_chain"), placebo_joint_p(regression1_placebo$type1, "chain_like")),
    `Origin-specific decay (Type 2)` = c(fmt_int(n_individuals_model(regression1_placebo$type2)), placebo_joint_p(regression1_placebo$type2, "small_site_chain"), placebo_joint_p(regression1_placebo$type2, "chain_like"))
  ),
  output = "tinytable"
) |>
  tinytable::theme_empty() |>
  tinytable::group_tt(
    j = list("Dependent variable: log hourly wage in main job" = 2:4),
    i = b1_placebo_layout$groups
  ) |>
  tinytable::style_tt(i = -1, line = "t") |>
  tinytable::style_tt(i = 0, bold = FALSE, line = "b") |>
  tinytable::style_tt(i = b1_placebo_layout$headers, italic = TRUE) |>
  # Coefficient rows, then 1 fit row and 3 added rows
  tinytable::style_tt(i = b1_placebo_layout$coef_end, line = "b") |>
  tinytable::style_tt(i = b1_placebo_layout$coef_end + 4, line = "b") |>
  tinytable::style_tt(j = 1, align = "l") |>
  tinytable::style_tt(j = 2:4, align = "c") |>
  pair_se_rows(b1_placebo_layout$starts)
```

::: {.notes}
*Notes:* This table reports OLS estimates of @eq-employee-wage extended with interactions of the three owner shares with small-site chain and chain-like workplaces, as a robustness check. The dependent variable is the log hourly wage in the employee's main job. Each column represents a different weighting of the owner shares, namely no decay (Type 0, as in our main specification), pooled decay (Type 1) and origin-specific decay (Type 2). All columns include covariates for age, sex, origin group, casual or permanent employment, occupation, education, SEIFA decile, occupational tenure, employer tenure and union membership, and year, industry-year and state-year fixed effects. Reference categories are managers and administrators (occupation), Year 11 or below (education), native-born (origin), casual employment and no union membership. The joint tests report the p-value of a Wald test of the null hypothesis that the three owner-share interactions for that workplace type are jointly zero. All standard errors reported in parentheses are clustered at the individual and industry-year levels. ∗ p < 0.10, ∗∗ p < 0.05, ∗∗∗ p < 0.01.
:::

```{r}

::: {.notes}
*Notes:* This table reports OLS estimates of @eq-employee-wage with small workplaces defined as having fewer than 20 people. These are the full results of @tbl-b1-main. The dependent variable is the log hourly wage in the employee's main job. Each column represents a different weighting of the owner shares, namely no decay (Type 0, $\lambda = 0$), pooled decay (Type 1, $\lambda = `r lambda_mean`$) and origin-specific decay (Type 2, $\lambda_{\text{MES}} = `r lambda_mes`$ and $\lambda_{\text{MNES}} = `r lambda_other`$). All columns include covariates for age, sex, origin group, casual or permanent employment, occupation, education, SEIFA decile, occupational tenure, employer tenure and union membership, and year, industry-year and state-year fixed effects. Reference categories are managers and administrators (occupation), Year 11 or below (education), native-born (origin), casual employment and no union membership. The F-statistic, with its degrees of freedom in parentheses, tests the null hypothesis that the three owner-share interactions are jointly zero, using the clustered covariance matrix; its p-value is reported in the row below. All standard errors reported in parentheses are clustered at the individual and industry-year levels. ∗ p < 0.10, ∗∗ p < 0.05, ∗∗∗ p < 0.01.
:::

::: {.notes}
*Notes:* This table reports OLS estimates of an alternative to @eq-employee-wage that replaces the three origin-specific owner shares with the share of all migrant owners, $\text{MO}^{(-i)}_{kt}$, and the share of low-English migrant owners, $\text{LEMO}^{(-i)}_{kt}$,

$$
\begin{aligned}
\log w_{it} = {} & \delta_t + \mu_{kt} + \nu_{rt} \\
& + \beta_1 \text{SmallSingleSite}_{it} + \beta_2 \text{SmallSiteChain}_{it} + \beta_3 \text{ChainLike}_{it} \\
& + \beta_4 \left(\text{SmallSingleSite}_{it} \times \text{MO}^{(-i)}_{kt}\right) + \beta_5 \left(\text{SmallSingleSite}_{it} \times \text{LEMO}^{(-i)}_{kt}\right) \\
& + \mathbf{X}'_{it}\boldsymbol{\pi} + \epsilon_{it},
\end{aligned}
$$

where $\text{MO}^{(-i)}_{kt}=\frac{\sum_{m \in (k,t), m\neq i} \omega_{mt} \text{Owner}_{mt} \text{Migrant}_m}{\sum_{m \in (k,t), m\neq i} \omega_{mt} \text{Owner}_{mt}}$ and $\text{LEMO}^{(-i)}_{kt}=\frac{\sum_{m \in (k,t), m\neq i} \omega_{mt} \text{Owner}_{mt} \text{Migrant}_m \text{LowEnglish}_m}{\sum_{m \in (k,t), m\neq i} \omega_{mt} \text{Owner}_{mt}}$ are leave-one-out shares in industry $k$ and year $t$, without decay. Low-English owners are also migrants, so $\beta_5$ measures how the small single-site gap changes with the share of low-English owners over and above the share of migrant owners. The dependent variable is the log hourly wage in the employee's main job. Each column represents a different level at which the industry cells, and so the owner shares and industry-year fixed effects, are defined, namely the 19 one-digit ANZSIC divisions used throughout, or two-digit ANZSIC industries. All columns include covariates for age, sex, origin group, casual or permanent employment, occupation, education, SEIFA decile, occupational tenure, employer tenure and union membership, and year, industry-year and state-year fixed effects. Reference categories are managers and administrators (occupation), Year 11 or below (education), native-born (origin), casual employment and no union membership. The F-statistic, with its degrees of freedom in parentheses, tests the null hypothesis that the two owner-share interactions are jointly zero, using the clustered covariance matrix; its p-value is reported in the row below. All standard errors reported in parentheses are clustered at the individual and one-digit industry-year levels. ∗ p < 0.10, ∗∗ p < 0.05, ∗∗∗ p < 0.01.
:::

### Inference with Few Industry Clusters {#sec-appendix-wild}

```{r}

main_se <- \(share) sprintf("%.3f", fixest::se(regression1_v1a)[[wild_term(share)]])
```

The owner shares in @eq-employee-wage vary only across the 19 one-digit industries and the years within them, and they change slowly within an industry. The standard errors in @tbl-b1-main are clustered by individual and by industry-year. This allows the errors of employees in the same industry and year to be correlated, but treats different years of the same industry as independent. If the errors have a persistent industry component, for example because small firms in some industries pay well for reasons that the controls do not capture, then both the owner shares and the errors are correlated across the years of an industry, and these standard errors understate the uncertainty [@moulton_illustration_1990].

Clustering by industry allows for this correlation, but it creates a second problem. After the fixed effects are partialled out, the cluster-robust variance estimator is

$$
\hat{V} = (X'X)^{-1}\left(\sum_{g=1}^{G} X_g'\hat{u}_g\hat{u}_g'X_g\right)(X'X)^{-1},
$$ {#eq-crve}

where $X_g$ and $\hat{u}_g$ are the regressors and residuals of industry $g$. With $G = 19$, the middle term is built from only 19 outer products. The estimator is consistent only as the number of clusters grows. With few clusters it is biased downward, because least squares fits each cluster's residuals partly to its own data, and the resulting t-statistics have thicker tails than the normal distribution. Conventional tests therefore reject a true null hypothesis too often [@cameron_bootstrap_2008].

To address this problem, we use the wild cluster bootstrap with the null hypothesis imposed [@cameron_bootstrap_2008]. To test $H_0: \beta_j = 0$, we first estimate @eq-employee-wage with $\beta_j$ set to zero, which gives the restricted fitted values $X_g\tilde{\beta}$ and residuals $\tilde{u}_g$. We then construct $B = 9{,}999$ bootstrap samples,

$$
y^{*b}_g = X_g\tilde{\beta} + v^{b}_g\,\tilde{u}_g, \qquad g = 1, \dots, G, \quad b = 1, \dots, B,
$$ {#eq-wild}

where $v^{b}_g$ is drawn independently for each industry from the six-point distribution of @webb_reworking_2023, which takes the values $\pm\sqrt{1/2}$, $\pm 1$ and $\pm\sqrt{3/2}$ with equal probability. In each sample we re-estimate the unrestricted model and compute the t-statistic $t^{*b}_j$ with the industry-clustered variance of @eq-crve. The bootstrap p-value is the share of these t-statistics that are at least as large in absolute value as the t-statistic $\hat{t}_j$ from the data,

$$
p^{*}_j = \frac{1}{B}\sum_{b=1}^{B} \mathbf{1}\left[\,\left|t^{*b}_j\right| \ge \left|\hat{t}_j\right|\,\right].
$$

The joint test is constructed in the same way, with all three interactions set to zero and the Wald statistic in place of the t-statistic.

The procedure addresses both problems. First, every observation of an industry is multiplied by the same $v^{b}_g$, which has mean zero and variance one. Each bootstrap sample therefore keeps the correlation of the errors within an industry, across workers and across years, while industries remain independent. Second, $t^{*b}_j$ is computed with the same estimator and the same 19 clusters as $\hat{t}_j$, so the bootstrap distribution inherits the downward bias and the thick tails of the clustered t-statistic. We compare $\hat{t}_j$ with this distribution instead of the normal distribution, so we do not need the clustered standard error itself to be accurate. Imposing the null hypothesis ensures that the bootstrap samples are generated under the hypothesis being tested.

@tbl-b1-wild reports the results. Clustering by industry roughly doubles the standard errors of the MES and high-English interactions, from `r main_se("mes")` to `r wild_se("mes")` and from `r main_se("mnes_higheng")` to `r wild_se("mnes_higheng")`, which indicates that the errors are correlated across the years of an industry. Under the wild cluster bootstrap, the high-English interaction remains significant at the 5 per cent level ($p `r wild_p("mnes_higheng")`$), while the MES interaction ($p `r wild_p("mes")`$) and the joint test of all three interactions ($p `r fmt_p_eq(wild0$p_wild[wild0$term == "joint"])`$) are not significant. The low-English interaction is insignificant under both approaches ($p `r wild_p("mnes_loweng")`$). The narrowing of the small single-site wage gap where high-English MNES owners are common is therefore robust to correlation within industries, but the MES interaction is not. The bootstrap is least reliable for the low-English interaction, because that share is zero in most industry-years and its variation comes from a few industries [@mackinnon_wild_2018].

```{r}
#| label: tbl-b1-wild
#| tbl-cap: "Owner-share interactions with p-values that cluster by industry (wild cluster bootstrap)."
#| echo: false

b1_wild_models <- list(type0 = regression1_v1a, type1 = regression1_v1b, type2 = regression1_v1c)

b1_wild_table <- purrr::map_dfr(names(b1_wild_models), \(type) {
  m <- b1_wild_models[[type]]
  w <- dplyr::filter(regression1_wild, type == !!type)
  terms <- w$term[w$term != "joint"]
  ct <- fixest::coeftable(m)
  joint <- cluster_f_test(m, paste(terms, "= 0"))
  tibble::tibble(
    `Owner share` = c(
      "Small single-site x MES owner share",
      "Small single-site x MNES high-English owner share",
      "Small single-site x MNES low-English owner share",
      "All three interactions jointly"
    ),
    Coefficient = c(sprintf("%.3f", ct[terms, 1]), ""),
    `p-value, individual and industry-year clusters` = c(fmt_p(ct[terms, 4]), fmt_p(joint[2, "Pr(>F)"])),
    `Standard error, industry clusters` = c(sprintf("%.3f", w$se_industry[seq_along(terms)]), ""),
    `Wild bootstrap p-value, industry clusters` = fmt_p(w$p_wild)
  )
})

b1_wild_table |>
  tinytable::tt(width = c(0.36, 0.12, 0.18, 0.16, 0.18)) |>
  tinytable::theme_empty() |>
  tinytable::group_tt(i = list(
    "No decay (Type 0)" = 1,
    "Pooled decay (Type 1)" = 5,
    "Origin-specific decay (Type 2)" = 9
  )) |>
  tinytable::style_tt(i = 0, line = "tb") |>
  tinytable::style_tt(i = c(1, 6, 11), italic = TRUE) |>
  tinytable::style_tt(i = 15, line = "b") |>
  tinytable::style_tt(j = 1, align = "l") |>
  tinytable::style_tt(j = 2:5, align = "c")
```

::: {.notes}
*Notes:* This table reports the owner-share interactions of @tbl-b1-main with p-values from two clustering schemes, with one panel for each weighting of the owner shares. *p-value, individual and industry-year clusters* is from the standard errors of @tbl-b1-main, and for the joint row from its F-test. The last two columns cluster at the industry level instead, which allows the errors of all years of an industry to be correlated. *Standard error, industry clusters* is the conventional clustered standard error with 19 industry clusters. *Wild bootstrap p-value, industry clusters* is from a wild cluster bootstrap that imposes the null hypothesis [@cameron_bootstrap_2008], with the six-point weights of @webb_reworking_2023 and 9,999 replications. For the joint row, the null is that all three interactions are zero.
:::

### Owner Shares Built with the Longitudinal Weight {#sec-appendix-lnw}

```{r}
#| include: false

# Share of owner person-years (waves 2 to 21) with a positive longitudinal
# weight, quoted in the text below
b1_lnw_owners <- panel_final |>
  dplyr::filter(
    dplyr::coalesce(is_owner == 1L, FALSE),
    !is.na(origin_group),
    as.integer(as.character(wave)) <= 21
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    wave_num = as.integer(as.character(wave)),
    has_lnw = dplyr::coalesce(responding_person_longitudinal_weight_lnwtrp, 0) > 0
  )
b1_lnw_cover <- c(
  all = mean(b1_lnw_owners$has_lnw[b1_lnw_owners$wave_num >= 2]),
  mnes_loweng = mean(b1_lnw_owners$has_lnw[b1_lnw_owners$origin_group == "mnes_loweng" & b1_lnw_owners$wave_num >= 2])
)
b1_lnw_persons <- b1_lnw_owners |>
  dplyr::filter(origin_group == "mnes_loweng") |>
  dplyr::summarise(all = dplyr::n_distinct(xwaveid), with_weight = dplyr::n_distinct(xwaveid[has_lnw])) |>
  unlist()
# Low-English interaction under each weight, quoted in the text below
b1_le <- \(m, term) sprintf("%.3f", coef(m)[[term]])
b1_le_p <- \(m, term) fmt_p_eq(fixest::pvalue(m)[[term]])
b1_le_term <- "small_single_site:loo_mnes_loweng_1d_type0"
```

Our main owner shares weight each owner by the HILDA cross-sectional responding-person weight, because each share describes the owners of an industry in a single wave. As a sensitivity check, @tbl-b1-lnw re-estimates the main specification and the two decay weightings with the shares weighted instead by the longitudinal responding-person weight. The decay rates are calibrated on these shares by an earlier version of the cross-validation in @sec-loo-shares, which used a narrower employee sample and did not control for the worker's origin, giving $\lambda = `r lambda_mean_lnw`$ for Type 1 and $\lambda_{\text{MES}} = `r lambda_mes_lnw`$ and $\lambda_{\text{MNES}} = `r lambda_other_lnw`$ for Type 2. This weight is zero in wave 1 and positive only for people who have responded in every wave since wave 1, so it gives weight to a shrinking subset of owners. Over waves 2 to 21 it is positive for `r fmt_num(100 * b1_lnw_cover[["all"]], 0)` per cent of owner person-years, but for only `r fmt_num(100 * b1_lnw_cover[["mnes_loweng"]], 0)` per cent of the person-years of low-English owners, and for `r b1_lnw_persons[["with_weight"]]` of the `r b1_lnw_persons[["all"]]` low-English owners observed in waves 1 to 21.

Without decay, the MES and high-English interactions have the same signs and similar sizes under both weights. The low-English interaction does not. Without decay it is $`r b1_le(regression1_lnw$type0, paste0(b1_le_term, "_lnw"))`$ ($p `r b1_le_p(regression1_lnw$type0, paste0(b1_le_term, "_lnw"))`$) with the longitudinal weight but $`r b1_le(regression1_v1a, b1_le_term)`$ ($p `r b1_le_p(regression1_v1a, b1_le_term)`$) with the cross-sectional weight (@tbl-b1-main), and the wild cluster bootstrap finds it insignificant under both weights (@tbl-b1-wild and @tbl-b1-lnw). The estimate for low-English owners therefore depends on which few owners receive weight, and we do not treat it as evidence in either direction.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-b1-lnw
#| tbl-cap: "Employee wage results with owner shares weighted by the longitudinal survey weight (sensitivity check)."
#| echo: false

# Main results with the owner shares weighted by the longitudinal weight
# (lnwtrp) instead of the cross-sectional weight, with decay rates calibrated
# on the lnwtrp-weighted shares
b1_lnw_types <- c(
  "No decay (Type 0)" = "type0",
  "Pooled decay (Type 1)" = "type1",
  "Origin-specific decay (Type 2)" = "type2"
)
b1_lnw_models <- setNames(regression1_lnw[b1_lnw_types], names(b1_lnw_types))
b1_lnw_inter <- \(type) paste0(
  "small_single_site:", c("loo_mes_1d_", "loo_mnes_higheng_1d_", "loo_mnes_loweng_1d_"), type, "_lnw"
)

coef_b1_lnw <- c(
  "small_single_site" = "Small single-site",
  "chain_like" = "Chain-like",
  "small_site_chain" = "Small-site chain"
)
b1_lnw_groups <- c(mes = "MES", mnes_higheng = "MNES high-English", mnes_loweng = "MNES low-English")
for (g in names(b1_lnw_groups)) {
  for (type in b1_lnw_types) {
    coef_b1_lnw[paste0("small_single_site:loo_", g, "_1d_", type, "_lnw")] <-
      paste("Small single-site x", b1_lnw_groups[[g]], "owner density")
  }
}

b1_lnw_layout <- b1_full_layout(c(
  "Firm structure" = 3,
  "Interactions of firm structure with owner density" = 3
))

# Joint F-tests and wild bootstrap p-values, one column per specification
b1_lnw_f <- purrr::map(b1_lnw_types, \(type) {
  cluster_f_test(regression1_lnw[[type]], paste(b1_lnw_inter(type), "= 0"))
})
b1_lnw_wild <- \(k) purrr::map_chr(b1_lnw_types, \(type) {
  fmt_p(regression1_wild_lnw$p_wild[regression1_wild_lnw$type == type][k])
})
b1_lnw_rows <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  c(term = "Individuals", purrr::map_chr(b1_lnw_models, \(m) fmt_int(n_individuals_model(m)))),
  c(term = "Year FEs", setNames(rep("Yes", 3), names(b1_lnw_types))),
  c(term = "Industry-year FEs", setNames(rep("Yes", 3), names(b1_lnw_types))),
  c(term = "State-year FEs", setNames(rep("Yes", 3), names(b1_lnw_types))),
  c(term = "F-Statistic (df)", purrr::map_chr(b1_lnw_f, \(f) sprintf("%.3f (%d, %d)", f[2, "F"], f[2, "Df"], f[2, "Res.Df"]))),
  c(term = "F-test p-value", purrr::map_chr(b1_lnw_f, \(f) fmt_p(f[2, "Pr(>F)"]))),
  c(term = "Wild bootstrap p-value, MES", b1_lnw_wild(1)),
  c(term = "Wild bootstrap p-value, MNES high-English", b1_lnw_wild(2)),
  c(term = "Wild bootstrap p-value, MNES low-English", b1_lnw_wild(3)),
  c(term = "Wild bootstrap p-value, joint", b1_lnw_wild(4))
)

modelsummary::modelsummary(
  b1_lnw_models,
  coef_map = c(coef_b1_lnw, b1_controls),
  gof_map = gof_comma(tribble(
    ~raw            , ~clean                        , ~fmt ,
    "nobs"          , "Observations (person-years)" ,    0 ,
    "r.squared"     , "R-Squared"                   ,    3 ,
    "adj.r.squared" , "Adjusted R-Squared"          ,    3
  )),
  estimate = "{estimate}{stars}",
  statistic = "({std.error})",
  stars = thesis_stars,
  fmt = modelsummary::fmt_decimal(digits = 3, big.mark = ","),
  add_rows = b1_lnw_rows,
  output = "tinytable"
) |>
  tinytable::theme_empty() |>
  tinytable::group_tt(
    i = b1_lnw_layout$groups,
    j = list("Dependent variable: log hourly wage in main job" = 2:4)
  ) |>
  tinytable::style_tt(i = -1, line = "t") |>
  tinytable::style_tt(i = 0, bold = FALSE, line = "b") |>
  tinytable::style_tt(i = b1_lnw_layout$headers, italic = TRUE) |>
  # Rule under the coefficients, and at the bottom after 3 fit rows and 10 added rows
  tinytable::style_tt(i = b1_lnw_layout$coef_end + c(0, 13), line = "b") |>
  tinytable::style_tt(j = 1, align = "l") |>
  tinytable::style_tt(j = 2:4, align = "c") |>
  pair_se_rows(b1_lnw_layout$starts)
```

::: {.notes}
*Notes:* This table reports OLS estimates of @eq-employee-wage with each owner in the leave-one-out shares of @eq-loo-shares weighted by the HILDA longitudinal responding-person weight instead of the cross-sectional weight. This weight is zero in wave 1 and positive only for people who have responded in every wave since, so there are fewer observations than in @tbl-b1-main where no other owner in the industry-year has a positive weight. The dependent variable is the log hourly wage in the employee's main job. Each column represents a different weighting of the owner shares, with decay rates calibrated on the longitudinally weighted shares, namely no decay (Type 0), pooled decay (Type 1, $\lambda = `r lambda_mean_lnw`$) and origin-specific decay (Type 2, $\lambda_{\text{MES}} = `r lambda_mes_lnw`$ and $\lambda_{\text{MNES}} = `r lambda_other_lnw`$). All columns include covariates for age, sex, origin group, casual or permanent employment, occupation, education, SEIFA decile, occupational tenure, employer tenure and union membership, and year, industry-year and state-year fixed effects. Reference categories are managers and administrators (occupation), Year 11 or below (education), native-born (origin), casual employment and no union membership. The F-statistic, with its degrees of freedom in parentheses, tests the null hypothesis that the three owner-share interactions are jointly zero, using the clustered covariance matrix; its p-value is reported in the row below. The wild bootstrap p-values test each interaction, and all three jointly, with errors clustered at the industry level, as in @tbl-b1-wild. All standard errors reported in parentheses are clustered at the individual and industry-year levels. ∗ p < 0.10, ∗∗ p < 0.05, ∗∗∗ p < 0.01.
:::

```{r}

Each column represents a separate regression on the unrestricted or restricted sample, with the covariates and fixed effects of @tbl-b2-main. The last column is the number of distinct large employers in the restricted income regression. A dash marks the single low-English large employer, who is excluded from estimation. All standard errors reported in parentheses are clustered at the individual and industry-year levels. ∗ p < 0.10, ∗∗ p < 0.05, ∗∗∗ p < 0.01.
:::

*Notes:* This table reports the owner–employee gap for own-account workers (self-employed, or owners without employees, in small workplaces), relative to employees of small workplaces of the same origin, from the regressions of @eq-owner-inc in @tbl-b2-main. Panel A reports the gap, $\theta_O$ for the native-born and $\theta_O + \theta_{Og}$ for migrant group $g$. Panel B reports the difference from the native-born gap, $\theta_{Og}$, and Panel C its minimum detectable difference, $2.8 \times \text{SE}(\theta_{Og})$. The dependent variables are income in dollars, and volatility and large falls in percentage points. Each column represents a separate regression on the unrestricted or restricted sample, with the covariates and fixed effects of @tbl-b2-main. The last column is the number of distinct own-account workers in the restricted income regression. ::: {.notes}
*Notes:* This table reports OLS estimates of @eq-owner-inc. These are the full results of @tbl-b2-main and @tbl-b2-premium. The dependent variables are annual labour and business income at $t$ in dollars, income volatility (the absolute arc per cent change of @eq-volatility, 0 to 200) and an indicator for an income fall of 25 per cent or more, in shares (0.145 is 14.5 percentage points). Each column represents a separate regression; the first three use the unrestricted sample, which classifies individuals by their status at $t$, and the last three the restricted sample of individuals with the same status at $t-1$ and $t$. The owner-type rows are $\theta_S$, $\theta_L$ and $\theta_O$, the origin rows are $\gamma_g$ and the interaction rows are $\theta_{Sg}$, $\theta_{Lg}$ and $\theta_{Og}$; the owner–employee gap of group $g$ in @tbl-b2-main is the owner-type row plus the interaction row. All columns include year, industry-year and state-year fixed effects; the volatility and large-fall columns also include the prior income decile, which ranks average income over waves $t-5$ to $t-2$, with a separate category for individuals with fewer than two waves observed. The reference categories are native-born employees, decile 5 and Year 11 or below. The single low-English large employer is excluded, so that interaction is not estimated. The F-test, with its degrees of freedom in parentheses and its p-value in the row below, tests the null hypothesis that all origin by owner-type interactions are jointly zero, using the clustered covariance matrix. All standard errors reported in parentheses are clustered at the individual and industry-year levels. ∗ p < 0.10, ∗∗ p < 0.05, ∗∗∗ p < 0.01.
:::

## Entry into Business Ownership {#sec-appendix-b3}

This section reports unconditional entry rates, the full estimates behind @tbl-b3-main and the robustness checks discussed in @sec-results-block3.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-b3-sample
#| tbl-cap: "Transitions into business ownership by migrant and language proficiency group."
#| echo: false

# Variables for the standardisation: age bands and industry of most recent
# job at t-1 (the 19 ANZSIC divisions, i.e. 1-digit industry)
sample_b3 <- data_regression_3 |>
  mutate(
    age_band = cut(
      age_hgage,
      breaks = c(-Inf, 24, 34, 44, 54, 64, Inf),
      labels = c("15-24", "25-34", "35-44", "45-54", "55-64", "65+")
    ),
    industry_1d = industry_19categories_jbmi61_fe
  )

# Entry counts by origin group
entry_counts <- sample_b3 |>
  summarise(
    n_atrisk = n(),
    n_entries = sum(entry_owner == 1),
    .by = origin_group
  )

baseline <- entry_counts |> filter(origin_group == "native")

# Fisher exact test against the Australian-born baseline
entry_tests <- entry_counts |>
  mutate(
    rate = 100 * n_entries / n_atrisk,
    p_fisher = purrr::map2_dbl(
      n_entries,
      n_atrisk,
      ~ if (.y == baseline$n_atrisk) {
        NA_real_
      } else {
        fisher.test(matrix(
          c(
            .x,
            .y - .x,
            baseline$n_entries,
            baseline$n_atrisk - baseline$n_entries
          ),
          nrow = 2,
          byrow = TRUE
        ))$p.value
      }
    )
  )

# Homogeneity test across all four groups
chisq_b3 <- chisq.test(
  cbind(entry_counts$n_entries, entry_counts$n_atrisk - entry_counts$n_entries)
)

# Person-clustered bootstrap CI for each group's entry rate
# (resamples individuals, so repeated waves of the same person are respected)
boot_entry_ci <- function(dat, group, R = 2000, seed = 1) {
  set.seed(seed)
  per_person <- dat |>
    filter(origin_group == group) |>
    summarise(waves = n(), entries = sum(entry_owner == 1), .by = xwaveid)
  n_id <- nrow(per_person)
  rates <- replicate(R, {
    i <- sample.int(n_id, n_id, replace = TRUE)
    100 * sum(per_person$entries[i]) / sum(per_person$waves[i])
  })
  tibble::tibble(
    lo = quantile(rates, 0.025),
    hi = quantile(rates, 0.975)
  )
}

entry_ci <- entry_counts |>
  mutate(
    ci = purrr::map(as.character(origin_group), \(g) {
      boot_entry_ci(sample_b3, g)
    })
  ) |>
  tidyr::unnest(ci) |>
  select(origin_group, lo, hi)

# Entry rate standardised to the Australian-born age and industry mix. A logit
# of entry on origin, age band and industry is used, rather than cell-by-cell
# rates, because many origin x age x industry cells hold one or two people.
# Each group's standardised rate is its average predicted entry rate over the
# Australian-born person-pairs.
std_model <- glm(
  entry_owner ~ origin_group + age_band + industry_1d,
  family = binomial(), data = sample_b3
)
native_pairs <- filter(sample_b3, origin_group == "native")
standardised <- tibble::tibble(
  origin_group = factor(levels(sample_b3$origin_group), levels = levels(sample_b3$origin_group)),
  standardised_rate = vapply(levels(sample_b3$origin_group), \(g) {
    nd <- dplyr::mutate(native_pairs, origin_group = factor(g, levels = levels(sample_b3$origin_group)))
    100 * mean(predict(std_model, newdata = nd, type = "response"))
  }, numeric(1))
)

# Assemble the table
b3_group_labels <- c(
  native = "Australian-born",
  mes = "Migrant, main English-speaking country",
  mnes_higheng = "Migrant, other country, high English",
  mnes_loweng = "Migrant, other country, low English"
)

entry_tests |>
  left_join(entry_ci, by = "origin_group") |>
  left_join(standardised, by = "origin_group") |>
  mutate(origin_group = factor(origin_group, levels = names(b3_group_labels))) |>
  arrange(origin_group) |>
  transmute(
    Group = b3_group_labels[as.character(origin_group)],
    `At-risk person-pairs` = format(n_atrisk, big.mark = ","),
    Entries = format(n_entries, big.mark = ","),
    `Entry rate (%)` = sprintf("%.2f", rate),
    `95% CI` = sprintf("[%.2f, %.2f]", lo, hi),
    `p vs Australian-born` = if_else(
      is.na(p_fisher),
      "",
      fmt_p(p_fisher)
    ),
    `Standardised rate (%)` = sprintf("%.2f", standardised_rate)
  ) |>
  tinytable::tt() |>
  tinytable::theme_empty() |>
  tinytable::style_tt(j = 1, align = "l") |>
  tinytable::style_tt(j = 2:7, align = "c") |>
  tinytable::style_tt(i = 0, line = "tb") |>
  tinytable::style_tt(i = 4, line = "b")
```

::: {.notes}
*Notes:* This table reports unconditional entry into business ownership in the transition sample, by origin group. The entry rate is the percentage of at-risk person-pairs (not a business owner at $t-1$) in which the individual owns a business at $t$. The 95% confidence interval is from a bootstrap that resamples individuals (2,000 replications). *p vs Australian-born* is from a Fisher exact test; a chi-square test of equal rates across all groups gives p `r fmt_p_eq(chisq_b3$p.value)`. *Standardised rate* is the entry rate each group would have with the Australian-born mix of age band and industry of most recent job at $t-1$, computed as each group's average predicted entry rate over the Australian-born person-pairs from a logit of entry on origin group, age band and industry.
:::

```{r}
#| label: tbl-b3-full
#| tbl-cap: "Full estimation results for entry into business ownership between t−1 and $t$."
#| echo: false

models3_full <- list(
  "Origin only" = regression3_v1a,
  "Labour market only" = regression3_v2a,
  "Origin and labour market" = regression3_v3a,
  "Adding human capital" = regression3_v4a
)

# --- Coefficient labels, by panel ---------------------------------------------

# cm3_origin, cm3_labour, cm3_human, cm3_demog and cm3_house are in thesis_format.R
cm3_panels <- list(
  "Origin and English proficiency" = cm3_origin,
  "Labour-market position at t−1" = cm3_labour,
  "Human capital and job attributes at t−1" = cm3_human,
  "Demographics" = cm3_demog,
  "Household and location at t−1" = cm3_house
)
# Coefficient map and row positions of the panel headers and rules
b3_full_layout <- full_coef_layout(models3_full, cm3_panels)

# --- Wald tests: weak labour-market outcomes jointly zero ---------------------

push_wald <- function(m) {
  w <- wald_chisq(m, c("unemployed_l1", "nilf_l1", "low_wage_l1", "liquidity_l1"))
  sprintf("%.2f (%s)", w$stat, fmt_p(w$p))
}

# --- Individuals per model ----------------------------------------------------

n_ind <- function(m) {
  format(n_distinct(data_regression_3$xwaveid[fixest::obs(m)]), big.mark = ",")
}

rows3_full <- tibble::tribble(
  ~term,               ~`Origin only`,                      ~`Labour market only`,                      ~`Origin and labour market`,                      ~`Adding human capital`,
  "Individuals",       n_ind(regression3_v1a),      n_ind(regression3_v2a),      n_ind(regression3_v3a),      n_ind(regression3_v4a),
  "Year FEs",          "Yes",                       "Yes",                       "Yes",                       "Yes",
  "Industry-year FEs", "Yes",                       "Yes",                       "Yes",                       "Yes",
  "State-year FEs",    "Yes",                       "Yes",                       "Yes",                       "Yes",
  "Wald χ² (p-value)", "",
                       push_wald(regression3_v2a),
                       push_wald(regression3_v3a),
                       push_wald(regression3_v4a)
)

n_gof <- 3
last_row <- b3_full_layout$coef_end + n_gof + nrow(rows3_full)

# --- Table ----------------------------------------------------------------------

modelsummary::modelsummary(
  models3_full,
  coef_map = b3_full_layout$map,
  gof_map = gof_comma(tibble::tribble(
    ~raw,   ~clean,         ~fmt,
    "nobs", "Observations (person-pairs)", 0,
    "aic",  "AIC",          0,
    "bic",  "BIC",          0
  )),
  estimate = "{estimate}{stars}",
  statistic = "({std.error})",
  stars = thesis_stars,
  add_rows = rows3_full,
  output = "tinytable"
) |>
  tinytable::theme_empty() |>
  tinytable::group_tt(
    j = list("Dependent variable: entry into business ownership (logit)" = 2:5),
    i = b3_full_layout$groups) |>
  tinytable::style_tt(i = b3_full_layout$headers, italic = TRUE) |>
  tinytable::style_tt(i = c(0, b3_full_layout$coef_end, last_row), line = "b") |>
  tinytable::style_tt(j = 1, align = "l") |>
  tinytable::style_tt(j = 2:5, align = "c") |>
  tinytable::style_tt(i = -1, line = "t") |>
  pair_se_rows(b3_full_layout$starts)
```

::: {.notes}
*Notes:* This table reports logit estimates of @eq-transition. These are the full results of @tbl-b3-main. The dependent variable equals one if an individual who is not a business owner at $t-1$ is an own-account worker or employer at $t$. Each column adds regressors in steps, starting with origin group only, then labour-market position and liquidity at $t-1$ only, then both and finally both with education and employer tenure at $t-1$. All columns include year, industry-year and state-year fixed effects. Coefficients are log-odds. Reference categories are the Australian-born, employees who were not low-paid and not liquidity constrained at $t-1$, Year 11 or below as highest education, male, married, not a homeowner and living in a major city. The Wald χ² statistic, with its p-value in parentheses, tests the null hypothesis that the four labour-market and liquidity coefficients are jointly zero. All standard errors reported in parentheses are clustered at the individual level. ∗ p < 0.10, ∗∗ p < 0.05, ∗∗∗ p < 0.01.
:::

```{r}
#| label: tbl-b3-robust
#| tbl-cap: "Timing of labour market status and within-person estimates of entry into business ownership (logit coefficients)."
#| echo: false

b3_origins <- c(mes = "MES", mnes_higheng = "MNES high English", mnes_loweng = "MNES low English")
b3_push <- function(lag) c(
  setNames(paste0(c("Unemployed", "Bottom wage quintile"), " at t−", lag, ""), paste0(c("unemployed_l", "low_wage_l"), lag)),
  unlist(lapply(c("unemployed", "low_wage"), \(p) setNames(
    paste0(b3_origins, " x ", if (p == "unemployed") "Unemployed" else "Bottom wage quintile", " at t−", lag, ""),
    paste0("origin_group", names(b3_origins), ":", p, "_l", lag)
  )))
)

b3_robust_models <- list(
  "Status at t−1" = regression3_timing_l1,
  "Status at t−2" = regression3_timing_l2,
  "Status at t−1 and t−2" = regression3_timing_both,
  "With person means" = regression3_mundlak
)
# Full results, with every coefficient grouped into panels
b3_robust_layout <- full_coef_layout(b3_robust_models, list(
  "Push from the labour market, by origin" = c(b3_push(1), b3_push(2)),

modelsummary::modelsummary(

::: {.notes}
*Notes:* This table reports logit estimates of @eq-transition-het with labour market status measured at different times. The dependent variable equals one if an individual who is not a business owner at $t-1$ is an own-account worker or employer at $t$. The first three columns use the person-pairs whose labour market status is also observed two years before entry, so that differences between them reflect timing and not sample composition, and measure unemployment and low wages at $t-1$, at $t-2$ and at both. *With person means* uses the full transition sample and adds each individual's mean of the time-varying regressors, so that the $t-1$ coefficients compare an individual with themselves at other times [@mundlak_pooling_1978]. All columns include the covariates of @tbl-b3-het and year, industry-year and state-year fixed effects. Coefficients are log-odds, with reference categories as in @tbl-b3-full. The joint test reports the p-value of a Wald test of the null hypothesis that all origin by labour-market interactions in the column are jointly zero. All standard errors reported in parentheses are clustered at the individual level. ∗ p < 0.10, ∗∗ p < 0.05, ∗∗∗ p < 0.01.
:::

```{r}
#| label: tbl-b3-lpm
#| tbl-cap: "Linear probability models of entry into business ownership (percentage points)."
#| echo: false

b3_lpm_models <- list(
  "Origin only" = regression3_lpm_v1,
  "Labour market only" = regression3_lpm_v2,
  "Origin and labour market" = regression3_lpm_v3,
  "Adding human capital" = regression3_lpm_v4,
  "Origin × push" = regression3_lpm_het,
  "Origin × push, individual FEs" = regression3_lpm_het_fe
)

# The individual fixed-effects model names its interactions with fixest's i()
# ("origin_group::mes:unemployed_l1"), so both spellings map to the same row
b3_lpm_inter <- function(g, label) {
  out <- character()
  for (p in c("unemployed_l1", "low_wage_l1")) {
    lab <- paste0(label, " × ", if (p == "unemployed_l1") "Unemployed" else "Bottom wage quintile")
    out[paste0("origin_group", g, ":", p)] <- lab
    out[paste0("origin_group::", g, ":", p)] <- lab
  }
  out
}
cm3_lpm <- c(
  "origin_groupmes" = "MES",
  "origin_groupmnes_higheng" = "MNES high English",
  "origin_groupmnes_loweng" = "MNES low English",
  "unemployed_l1" = "Unemployed",
  "nilf_l1" = "Not in labour force",
  "low_wage_l1" = "Bottom wage quintile",
  "liquidity_l1" = "Liquidity constrained",
  b3_lpm_inter("mes", "MES"),
  b3_lpm_inter("mnes_higheng", "MNES high English"),
  b3_lpm_inter("mnes_loweng", "MNES low English")
)
# Interaction rows ordered by push, then group, as in @tbl-b3-robust
b3_lpm_inter_all <- cm3_lpm[grepl(":", names(cm3_lpm))]
b3_lpm_inter_all <- b3_lpm_inter_all[order(!grepl("unemployed_l1$", names(b3_lpm_inter_all)))]

# Full results, with every coefficient grouped into panels
b3_lpm_layout <- full_coef_layout(b3_lpm_models, list(
  "Origin and English proficiency" = cm3_origin,
  "Labour-market position at t−1" = cm3_labour,
  "Origin × labour-market position at t−1" = b3_lpm_inter_all,
  "Human capital and job attributes at t−1" = cm3_human,
  "Demographics" = cm3_demog,
  "Household and location at t−1" = cm3_house
))

b3_lpm_joint_p <- \(m) fmt_p(fixest::wald(m, keep = ":(unemployed|low_wage)_l1$", print = FALSE)$p)
b3_lpm_mean <- \(m) sprintf("%.2f", mean(fitted(m) + resid(m)))

b3_lpm_n <- \(m) fmt_int(nobs(m))

b3_lpm_rows <- tibble::tibble(
  term = c("Observations (person-pairs)", "Individuals", "Mean entry rate (%)", "Year, industry-year and state-year FEs",
           "Individual FEs", "Joint test of interactions (p-value)"),
  `Origin only` = c(b3_lpm_n(regression3_lpm_v1), fmt_int(n_individuals_model(regression3_lpm_v1)), b3_lpm_mean(regression3_lpm_v1), "Yes", "No", ""),
  `Labour market only` = c(b3_lpm_n(regression3_lpm_v2), fmt_int(n_individuals_model(regression3_lpm_v2)), b3_lpm_mean(regression3_lpm_v2), "Yes", "No", ""),
  `Origin and labour market` = c(b3_lpm_n(regression3_lpm_v3), fmt_int(n_individuals_model(regression3_lpm_v3)), b3_lpm_mean(regression3_lpm_v3), "Yes", "No", ""),
  `Adding human capital` = c(b3_lpm_n(regression3_lpm_v4), fmt_int(n_individuals_model(regression3_lpm_v4)), b3_lpm_mean(regression3_lpm_v4), "Yes", "No", ""),
  `Origin × push` = c(b3_lpm_n(regression3_lpm_het), fmt_int(n_individuals_model(regression3_lpm_het)), b3_lpm_mean(regression3_lpm_het), "Yes", "No", b3_lpm_joint_p(regression3_lpm_het)),
  `Origin × push, individual FEs` = c(b3_lpm_n(regression3_lpm_het_fe), fmt_int(n_individuals_model(regression3_lpm_het_fe)), b3_lpm_mean(regression3_lpm_het_fe), "Yes", "Yes", b3_lpm_joint_p(regression3_lpm_het_fe))
)

# Coefficient rows (with their panel headers), then the added rows
b3_lpm_last_coef <- b3_lpm_layout$coef_end
b3_lpm_last_row <- b3_lpm_last_coef + nrow(b3_lpm_rows)

modelsummary::modelsummary(
  b3_lpm_models,
  coef_map = b3_lpm_layout$map,
  gof_map = NA,
  estimate = "{estimate}{stars}",
  statistic = "({std.error})",
  stars = thesis_stars,
  fmt = modelsummary::fmt_decimal(digits = 3, big.mark = ","),

::: {.notes}
*Notes:* This table reports OLS estimates of linear probability versions of @eq-transition (first four columns) and @eq-transition-het (last two columns), on the same person-pairs as the logits in @tbl-b3-main and @tbl-b3-het. The dependent variable is 100 times the entry indicator, so each coefficient is a change in the annual probability of entry in percentage points. Each column matches the corresponding logit specification; the last column adds individual fixed effects, which absorb the origin groups, and drops individuals observed in only one person-pair. All columns include the covariates of the corresponding logit and year, industry-year and state-year fixed effects, with reference categories as in @tbl-b3-full. The joint test reports the p-value of a Wald test of the null hypothesis that the six origin by labour-market interactions are jointly zero. All standard errors reported in parentheses are clustered at the individual level. ∗ p < 0.10, ∗∗ p < 0.05, ∗∗∗ p < 0.01.
:::

```{r}
#| label: tbl-b3-push-shares
#| tbl-cap: "Labour market position and liquidity at t−1 among people at risk of entering business ownership, by origin group."
#| echo: false

push_vars <- c(
  unemployed_l1 = "Unemployed",
  nilf_l1 = "Not in labour force",
  low_wage_l1 = "Bottom wage quintile",
  liquidity_l1 = "Liquidity constrained"
)

# Liquidity is observed only for people who returned the self-completion
# questionnaire, so it uses those person-pairs alone
push_sample <- function(d, v) {
  if (v == "liquidity_l1") dplyr::filter(d, liquidity_miss_l1 == 0) else d
}

# Share of each group in each position, in percent
push_shares <- function(d) {
  out <- tibble::tibble(Group = unname(group_labels))
  for (v in names(push_vars)) {
    dv <- push_sample(d, v)
    s <- tapply(dv[[v]], dv$origin_group, mean)[names(group_labels)]
    out[[push_vars[[v]]]] <- ifelse(is.na(s), "–", sprintf("%.1f", 100 * s))
  }
  out
}

# Difference from the native-born in percentage points (07_analysisblock3.R)
push_diff <- regression3_push_position

# Each difference (with its stars) over its standard error
diff_rows <- tibble::tibble(Group = as.vector(rbind(unname(group_labels[-1]), "")))
for (v in names(push_vars)) {
  ct <- fixest::coeftable(push_diff[[v]])
  terms <- paste0("origin_group::", names(group_labels)[-1])
  diff_rows[[push_vars[[v]]]] <- as.vector(rbind(
    sprintf("%.1f%s", ct[terms, 1], add_stars(ct[terms, 4])),
    sprintf("(%.1f)", ct[terms, 2])
  ))
}

entrants <- dplyr::filter(data_regression_3, entry_owner == 1)
n_col <- function(d) fmt_int(as.integer(table(d$origin_group)[names(group_labels)]))

dplyr::bind_rows(
  dplyr::mutate(push_shares(data_regression_3), `Person-pairs` = n_col(data_regression_3)),
  dplyr::mutate(diff_rows, `Person-pairs` = ""),
  dplyr::mutate(push_shares(entrants), `Person-pairs` = n_col(entrants))
) |>
  dplyr::rename(" " = Group) |>
  tinytable::tt(width = c(0.25, rep(0.15, 4), 0.15)) |>
  tinytable::theme_empty() |>
  tinytable::group_tt(i = list(
    "Panel A: Share of person-pairs at risk of entry (%)" = 1,
    "Panel B: Difference from the native-born, adjusted (percentage points)" = 5,
    "Panel C: Share of entrants (%)" = 11
  )) |>
  tinytable::style_tt(i = 0, line = "tb") |>
  tinytable::style_tt(i = c(1, 6, 13), italic = TRUE) |>
  tinytable::style_tt(i = 17, line = "b") |>
  tinytable::style_tt(j = 1, align = "l") |>
  tinytable::style_tt(j = 2:6, align = "c") |>
  pair_se_rows(c(1, 5, 11))
```

::: {.notes}
*Notes:* This table reports labour market position and liquidity at $t-1$ by origin group, for person-pairs in the transition sample of @tbl-b3-main. Each column is an indicator defined in @sec-data-outcomes. Panel A reports the percentage of each group in each position. Panel B reports the difference from the native-born from an OLS regression of the indicator (multiplied by 100) on the origin groups, age, age squared, sex and year fixed effects, with standard errors clustered at the individual level in parentheses. Panel C repeats Panel A for the person-pairs in which the individual enters ownership at $t$, and rests on few low-English entries. Liquidity is observed only for respondents who returned the self-completion questionnaire, so its shares and differences use those person-pairs alone. ∗ p < 0.10, ∗∗ p < 0.05, ∗∗∗ p < 0.01.
